item.title: How New Jersey swapped delegates to back independence
item.description: The Dean’s List with Host Dean Bowen – In 1776, New Jersey faces a political crisis as its delegates oppose independence. Determined patriots respond by replacing them, reshaping the colony’s representation and future. Through behind-the-scenes maneuvering, key figures work to align New Jersey with the American cause, helping secure support for independence at a pivotal moment in history...

item.title: When medicine stops listening
item.description: America Out Loud PULSE with Dr. Randall Bock – Her experience reflects a broader pattern in modern medicine. Visits have expanded in scope while narrowing in purpose. Screening and risk inventories dominate encounters. Case-finding replaces diagnosis. Patients are evaluated for many things they did not come in for, while the problem that brought them there remains untouched...

item.title: Trump’s healthcare plan: Who decides when or if you get care now?
item.description: The Tenpenny Files – Healthcare decisions are quietly shifting away from doctors and patients into administrative systems that control approval, cost, and access. Twila Brase explains how insurer dominance, Medicare changes, and federal policy now determine when care moves forward. As delays increase and choices narrow, Americans discover too late that medical judgment has been replaced by bureaucratic control...

item.title: Would diseases return if vaccination campaigns stopped?
item.description: Would diseases like polio and measles return if vaccination campaigns stopped? This issue examines whether modern sanitation, surveillance, and medical treatment prevent large-scale outbreaks, and how unvaccinated individuals manage infections today. It also explores when targeted vaccination still makes sense under shared decision-making in developed nations...
